newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso closes steady in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso closes steady in quiet market.

text.p: The Philippine peso ended steady at26.374 in a quiet session on Monday as the Central Bank's 20 percent overnight borrowing rate injected calm in the market, traders said.
In late deals, however, the Central Bank sold some $10 million at 26.375, they said.
"Some are anticipating the Central Bank may still cut its overnight rate," a foreign bank dealer said. "Once that happens everyone will buy the dollar."
In recent days, the Central Bank had to raise its key rate several times and sell dollars to fight speculation against the peso caused by the problems of the Thai baht.
Others, however, believe the Central Bank would maintain its rate at 20 percent in the next few days in view of the May 20 meeting of the U.S. Federal Open Market Committee.
"He (the Central Bank) will maintain the rate until the dust settles," another said.
Volume thinned to $141 million from a record $655.5 million on Friday.
